Tokyo's Hero Business.name: Tokyo's Hero Business
Tokyo's Hero Business.description:
📸 Under the giant screens, heroes fight for camera time and the crowd films everything.

📍 Tokyo's scramble crossing · Monday morning
🎭 Flashy, busy, cynical underneath
👥 For Licensed Sidekicks, Licensed Pro Heroes and Civilian Life
Tokyo's Hero Business.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is Monday morning in central Tokyo, the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. Heroes treat this district as a stage: an arrest here can reach the evening news within the hour, and incident counts decide rankings and pay. The PC is either a licensed sidekick at a Tokyo agency, the one their background names or else a mid-sized agency fighting for camera time, or a civilian working near the crossing, as their Path states. A fan account posts live hero sightings, and a pickpocket crew uses it to work wherever the heroes are not. Informants sell rookie heroes early tips, and at least one has started causing small incidents to have something to sell. The ward office wants crowd-control rules after two agencies scuffled over an arrest on camera, and the police blame heroes who play to the crowd. Since the news that All Might now teaches, vans selling unlicensed All Might teacher goods park nearby and move every hour.

THE PLACE: The Scramble Crossing: a huge intersection where every crosswalk opens at once about every two minutes and thousands cross in all directions. Giant screens on four buildings show news, hero clips and ads. At this hour commuters own it. Police watch from a corner box, and licensed heroes stand on the corners to be seen. When an incident starts, the crowd turns and raises its phones before anyone runs. A chime sounds each time the signal changes.

THE MOMENT: The signal chimes and the crowd floods the crossing. All four screens cut at once to the same clip, All Might's grin over a headline about his first day of teaching, and thousands of heads tip up. In the stalled crowd a woman, Emiko Tanabe, shouts that her bag is gone, and the lights will change again in under two minutes.

WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Mirko: works Billboard Avenue a block away; solo, goes wherever the fight is, may leap in and take the arrest with a laugh.
- Edgeshot: on duty near the Department Stores; precise and courteous, credits others and states one plan in a few words.
- Yoroi Musha: an elderly veteran in full armor who plants himself and holds the line.
- Uwabami: a celebrity pro who films commercials for the broadcast center; her snakes find people the eye misses.
- Best Jeanist: heads a Tokyo agency; corrects posture and conduct in one calm breath, and his sidekicks wear fitted denim.
- Burnin: one of Endeavor's sidekicks, loud and blunt; the Endeavor agency competes on incident counts across the city.

OPENING HOOKS:
- Licensed Pro Hero: the PC's young agency has paid for one hour of corner time under the giant screens, and the rival agency's top sidekick is already posing in the PC's spot.
- Licensed Sidekick: the PC holds the agency's corner to be seen; a rival agency's sidekick holds the opposite one, and both radios call the same theft.
- Civilian Life: the PC is opening a shift at a shop window on the crossing, the manager, Takeshi Nomura, wants any hero arrest filmed to sell, and the thief runs straight past the counter.
- Family Business: an unlicensed All Might goods van has parked in front of the family shop's window, undercutting every price, and the vendor, Goro Iwata, smiles at the PC.
- Criminal Ties: the PC recognizes a lookout from a crew they know, and an informant at the PC's elbow offers a tip about an incident that has not happened yet.
- Mutant: the fan account's streamer, Aoi Fujita, fixes her livestream on the PC's heteromorph features, mistakes the PC for a famous hero and sends the crowd their way.
- Default: the screens, the stalled crowd, the shout; the clock on the signal is running, and the PC is closest.

RULES:
- Third person present tense. The opening stays at the Scramble Crossing until the player moves the PC.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; a civilian's public Quirk use is illegal except in self-defense, and street cameras cover every corner.
- Top heroes are themselves, busy and proud; none of them exists to rescue the PC's scene.
- Nothing of the year is promised or foreshadowed; outcomes stay open.
- End the opening on an open moment, not a question to the player.

THE FIRST DAYS: the crossing runs on a daily rhythm: commuters own the mornings, shoppers the afternoons, the nightlife the evenings, and the signal changes every two minutes through all of it. A sidekick's week is corner shifts, calls on the agency radio, reports and statements at the corner police box; a pro's week adds sponsor meetings, signings at the Department Stores and the cost of being seen; a civilian's week is shifts, rent, the subway and hero news on every screen.

HOW THE BUSINESS WORKS: arrests and rescues on camera feed incident counts, rankings and sponsorships. When two heroes reach one incident, the capture goes to whoever restrains the suspect, and arguing over it on camera costs both agencies. Police seize unlicensed goods and question the vendor. A hero can ask the crowd to step back, never take a phone.

PEOPLE TO KNOW (how they treat a newcomer, from their records):
- Mirko: sums a newcomer up in one sentence, respects anyone who keeps up, and takes the arrest if they hesitate.
- Edgeshot: the same courtesy to a junior as to a colleague; credits whoever did the work.
- Best Jeanist: corrects a newcomer's posture, language and attitude in one calm breath.
- Uwabami: sees a newcomer as a brand, a rival for screen time, or both.
- Yoroi Musha: formal and restrained; holds the line and says little.
- Burnin: loud pep talks and blunt opinions for anyone near her.

WHAT THE PC CAN DO: chase the thief through the crowd, ask Emiko Tanabe what was taken and which way he went, call the police box, hold their corner, work with the rival or race them, or, as a civilian, shout a description, film, or stay at the counter. Every choice is the player's.

MORE RULES:
- The opening needs no fight: a returned bag or a clear witness statement completes the scene.
- A civilian PC who grabs the thief by hand still gives a statement at the corner box; using a Quirk to do it brings police questions as well.
- The fan account and the pickpocket crew are a lead, not a solved case: the link is proven one witness, post and face at a time.
Tokyo's Hero Business.firstQuest: Make a living in the capital's hero business without letting it make a fool or a crook of the PC: find out who profits when the crowd looks up.
Tokyo's Hero Business.questGenerationGuidance: Favor the business side of heroics in Tokyo. Agencies fighting for camera time and incident counts; staged incidents sold by informants; the pickpocket crew and the fan account that feeds it; unlicensed merchandise vans and the police chasing them; ward rules on crowd control; sponsorships, commercials and the ranking chase; footage sellers and reporters. For civilians: shifts, rent, a manager's schemes, a shop to protect, a witness statement that matters. Top pros such as Mirko, Edgeshot, Best Jeanist and Uwabami pass through on their own business, as allies, rivals or judges. Canon events arrive only when their causes are in place and are never resolved off-screen. Stakes are money, reputation, a job, and the line between a hero and a performer. Early work stays small and paid: one shift, one corner, one sponsor, one informant's price, one bag returned.
